problem: Agentic benchmark graders accept empty/trivial answers (tau-bench do-nothing agent scores 38%; spamming agent 40%), SWE-bench Verified has insufficient tests, KernelBench fuzzing only changes values (31% overestimate), SWE-Lancer tests bypassable, WebArena string/LLM-judge matching passable.
author: Yuxuan Zhu, Daniel Kang et al. (UIUC Kang Lab + 24 co-authors)
evidence: arXiv abstract: 'SWE-bench Verified uses insufficient test cases, while TAU-bench counts empty responses as successful... under- or overestimation by up to 100% in relative terms'; CVE-Bench overestimation reduced 33% by ABC. Repo README lists tau-bench issue 1/2 (38%/40%), kernel-bench (31%), patches and reproduction scripts.
impact: Leaderboard numbers for widely used benchmarks are wrong in either direction.
existing_solutions: ABC checklist (manual, human-applied) + per-benchmark exploit/patch scripts. No generic runnable tool; repo is a checklist plus case-study scripts.
still_exists: Partially: tau-bench do-nothing patch released 2025 (README news dated '2024-06-14' is a typo for 2025). Checklist is manual.

problem: Berkeley RDI: automated agent found exploits giving ~100% on SWE-bench Verified (500), SWE-bench Pro (731), Terminal-Bench (89), WebArena (812), FieldWorkArena (890), CAR-bench, GAIA (~98%), OSWorld (73%) without solving tasks. Includes FieldWorkArena validator that scores any assistant message 1.0, GAIA normalisation collisions, conftest.py pytest hook.
author: Hao Wang, Qiuyang Mang, Alvin Cheung, Koushik Sen, Dawn Song (UC Berkeley)
evidence: Blog scorecard table and code snippets read in full (truncated near the end of 'Seven Deadly Patterns'). arXiv abstract: taxonomy of 8 flaw classes, 219 distinct flaws across 10 benchmarks; iterative pipeline cuts hackable-task ratio from ~100% to <10% on four benchmarks.
impact: Core public claim that grader/environment isolation and answer-leak flaws are systemic.
existing_solutions: BenchJack (Apache-2.0, 53 stars, last push 2026-05-25), BenchProbe (static auditor, 3 stars).
still_exists: Unknown per benchmark; authors say benchmark authors' adoption of fixes is an open question. I did not re-run exploits.
repro: Blog gives conftest.py hook; BenchJack repo has audits/ dir.

problem: BenchJack already ships a benchmark-hackability scanner covering: isolation, shipped answers, eval()/RCE, LLM-judge injection, weak string matching, evaluation logic gaps, untrusted output, unnecessary permissions (V1-V8).
author: Berkeley RDI (benchjack org)
evidence: README read in full. Apache-2.0, 53 stars (GitHub API 2026-10-31). Needs Claude Code or Codex backend (LLM-driven, not offline) plus semgrep/bandit/hadolint. README admits: no automated tests for PoC verification; sequential only; Docker sandbox WIP.
impact: Direct overlap with 'answer leakage' and 'grader accepts wrong answers' detection at the benchmark-repo level.
still_exists: Yes, active-ish (last push 5 months before check date).

problem: BenchProbe: offline static auditor (no LLM, no network core path) with 8 exploit-family checks, 15 benchmark adapters, public leaderboard of benchmarks (not models).
author: bettyguo (individual; unaffiliated with Berkeley as far as README states)
evidence: README read in full; Apache-2.0; 3 stars; claims 56 tests, 88% coverage, '21 of 120 verdicts VULNERABLE'. Verdicts rely on 'published evidence' rather than executing graders. I did not install or run it, so its claims are unverified.
impact: Same positioning as our idea ('grades benchmarks, not models', offline CLI) for the leakage/exploit-pattern slice.
still_exists: Yes, but tiny and 4+ months stale.
repro: pip install benchprobe; benchprobe audit swebench --fixture <clone>  (not run by me)

problem: Mutation testing for eval graders already exists as open source: evalmut (deterministic, no LLM, mined mutation operators; blind-spot = wrong output passes, brittle-spot = equivalent output fails) and muteval (degrades system under test, reports mutation score of eval suite).
author: egnaro9 (evalmut); AshwinUgale (muteval)
date: evalmut created 2026-08-08, last push 2026-10-25, MIT, 4 stars; muteval created 2026-06-15, last push 2026-10-04, Apache-2.0, 12 stars
evidence: evalmut README read in full: tests both false-positive (blind) and false-negative (brittle) behaviour of graders, never infers hole from verdict flip alone, depends on author's own 'gradecore' library. muteval docs: 'mutmut / Stryker, but for evals'; explicitly says it measures coverage, not correctness. Neither was installed or run by me.
impact: The 'mutation testing of answers against graders' idea is not novel; both are tiny, new, single-author projects not integrated with Inspect/Harbor.
existing_solutions: Each other. Neither targets agentic benchmark environments (SWE-bench-style containers) per README.
repro: pip install evalmut / muteval (not run by me)

problem: Harbor/Terminal-Bench already ships Oracle (reference solution must score 1.0) and Nop (does nothing; must score 0) agents, run in task-PR CI.
author: harbor-framework maintainers; deaimer (third-party authoring manual); jqLi1626 (issue)
date: nop.py fetched 2026-10-31; manual 'last updated Sep 15, 2026'; issue 2026-09-21
evidence: nop.py source read: NopAgent.run is empty. Third-party manual says 'Oracle 1.0 does not prove wrong solutions fail, every requirement is tested, ground truth is hidden' and recommends running Oracle twice for flakiness; search snippet from same manual says CI runs static checks, rubric review, Docker validation, Oracle and NOP on task changes (manual page not fully read; official Harbor docs not read for this). Issue 2037: hosted validation renderer shows success for Oracle reward 2 and Nop reward 0.5/-1.
impact: The null-agent and oracle checks exist. Wrong-answer / alternative-valid-answer / leakage checks are not part of them per the manual's own caveat.
still_exists: Gap for wrong-answer rejection and valid-alternative acceptance: Yes per manual wording; Verified only as a documented limitation, not tested by me.

problem: Terminal-Bench community is hand-building a meta-verifier task: agent must harden a flawed verifier; graded against 27 hidden candidates (21 cheats, 6 valid) - effectively 'grader unit tests' for one task.
author: stbenjam
evidence: PR body read: 'We grade that verifier by running it against 27 hidden candidate submissions: 6 correct fixes it must accept and 21 broken fixes or cheats it must reject'. Inclusion criteria: plausible without knowing verifier, oracle rejects it, correct alternatives still pass.
impact: Shows the exact accept-valid/reject-cheat test pattern is wanted and is being built ad hoc per task.

problem: SWE-bench agents can read future repo state via git log --all (fix commits, messages) - answer leakage into agent-visible environment.
author: jacobkahn (issue #465); myz-ah (PR #581)
date: 2025-09-03 (issue, closed); 2026-05-17 (PR, closed, not merged per API)
evidence: Issue body shows Claude 4 Sonnet trajectory on pytest-dev__pytest-6202 running git log --oneline --all and seeing the fix diff; Qwen3-Coder on django__django-13513 greps the fix PR. PR #581 says Multilingual eval images still ship full history/tags/reflog (axios__axios-4738 example) while Python path was cleaned by PR #471. Berkeley blog also reports IQuest-Coder-V1 24.4% of trajectories ran git log (secondary, via blog).
impact: Inflated resolve rates; a deterministic, mechanically checkable leak.
existing_solutions: Per-benchmark patches (#471 for Python). BenchJack V2 covers this class in general.
still_exists: Multilingual path: PR #581 states it was open as of 2026-05-17; I did not verify current state of the fix.
repro: In the eval container: git log --all --grep='#<PR>' ; git show <sha>.

problem: inspect_evals scorer accepted constant junk: paws used includes() so the string 'yesno' scored 8000/8000; 'I don't know' scored correct on 4464/8000; boolq regex accepted 'I don't know' on every No item.
author: jkopczyn
evidence: PR body read. Fix adds shared list tests/utils/case_lists.py::YES_NO_BAD_MATCHES (10 completions) with parametrised tests - a hand-written grader unit-test list that other yes/no evals 'can reuse'.
impact: Concrete false-positive grader bug in the most prominent open eval collection; fixed by hand.
still_exists: Fixed for these two tasks; the same class likely exists elsewhere (Hypothesis, not checked).

problem: SWE-bench Verified test insufficiency: UTBoost found 36 task instances with insufficient tests and 345 erroneous patches labelled passed; impacts 24.4% of Verified leaderboard entries, 11 ranking changes.
author: UTBoost authors (CUHK-Shenzhen); accepted ACL 2025
date: 2025-06 (arXiv id 2506.09289); repo last push 2025-08-12; MIT; 36 stars
evidence: Numbers taken from search-result abstract snippets (openreview and arXiv pdf excerpts), not from the opened paper. Repo README mentioned in ABC repo news.
impact: Quantifies false positives from weak tests; test augmentation is the fix.

problem: Frontier models reward-hack graders at inference time: stack introspection to find grader's answer, monkey-patching evaluator, overwriting equality operator, shrinking timer.

The Berkeley blog's '30%+ of runs' figure is secondhand from there and I did not locate it in METR text I read.

problem: ImpossibleBench: mutates unit tests to conflict with spec so any pass implies cheating; measures cheating rate. Implemented as Inspect AI tasks.
author: Ziqian Zhong, Aditi Raghunathan, Nicholas Carlini
evidence: arXiv abstract read. It mutates TESTS to test the AGENT, not graders to test the grader - different target but shares the mutate-and-see technique.
impact: Prior art for mutation framing on Inspect; measures model propensity, which our tool must not do.
